method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis' (published 11 September 2024), 16 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC11534099). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from World Scleroderma Foundation GI ad hoc committee (Hughes M, Cricchio AL, De Santis MC, et al.), Journal of Scleroderma and Related Disorders 11(1):e000024 (doi 10.1136/jsrd-2026-000024) 'Expert recommendations for the management of refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease in systemic sclerosis: A report from the World Scleroderma Foundation (WSF) Gastrointestinal 'Ad hoc committee'' (published 1 January 2026), 12 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC (per Europe PMC); the PMC copy is the NIH author manuscript (NIHMS2140814), 'available for text mining' and fair use (read at Europe PMC search record (license field) and the <license> element of the NCBI efetch JATS XML for PMC13271578). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the World Scleroderma Foundation 2026 expert recommendations on refractory reflux in SSc (NIH author manuscript, JATS XML from NCBI efetch because the Europe PMC full-text service returned 500), paraphrased and hash-anchored. The S1 claims and anchors are unchanged from edition 1.0. Table rows appended with pmc_text.py --append-tables (2026-09-24); claims from S2 Table 1 (general approach) are paraphrased and anchored to its row lines. S2 Tables 2 and 4 restate recommendations already on the page; S2 Tables 3 and 5 have merged cells and were not extracted. S1 has no tables in its XML.

claims.claim: **The gut is the organ most often involved in SSc**, and GI symptoms are among the most burdensome for patients, adults and children alike.
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reflux oesophagitis often responds to acid suppression, but dysmotility and anorectal disease with incontinence are much harder to treat.** Gastroenterology and, when needed, GI surgical input can transform outcomes.
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Nutrition matters**: many people struggle to eat enough, and dietary changes can help both gut and general disease.
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Optimise and check adherence to general and lifestyle measures** for oesophageal symptoms such as reflux. (1C, 99%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Use a proton pump inhibitor and/or an H2-receptor antagonist for symptomatic reflux and dysphagia.** (1C, 99%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prokinetics (for example dopamine-antagonist promotility drugs) may be added** for dysphagia and reflux. (1C, 98%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If reflux is refractory**, investigate upper GI structure and motility and confirm acid reflux, for example with pH testing. (2C, 96%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Barrett's metaplasia is common in SSc** and, with other risk factors, should prompt follow-up gastroscopy; a history of Barrett's oesophagus marks a high-risk case for follow-up cancer screening. (2C, 94%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In SSc lung disease, manage reflux as part of supportive care**; oesophageal involvement may limit eligibility for lung transplant.
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refractory reflux in SSc (WSF):** symptoms, or new or continuing mucosal disease (Barrett's, oesophagitis, strictures, ulcers, even without symptoms), despite optimal acid suppression. Optimal means a high-dose PPI (omeprazole 40 mg or more a day or equivalent, for example twice daily) or a combination such as PPI plus H2 blocker or standard-dose PPI plus a promotility drug; standard dose is omeprazole 20 mg a day.
claims.locator: World Scleroderma Foundation GI ad hoc committee (Hughes M, Cricchio AL, De Santis MC, et al.), Journal of Scleroderma and Related Disorders 11(1):e000024 (doi 10.1136/jsrd-2026-000024), 'Expert recommendations for the management of refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease in systemic sclerosis: A report from the World Scleroderma Foundation (WSF) Gastrointestinal 'Ad hoc committee'', published 1 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13271578/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Look for red flags** (iron-deficiency anaemia, unintended weight loss, night sweats, fever) that need urgent tests for cancer, infection or bleeding. In early diffuse or anti-RNA polymerase III-positive disease, remember gastric antral vascular ectasia ('watermelon stomach') as a bleeding source. Finish the work-up before blaming SSc for GI symptoms.
claims.locator: World Scleroderma Foundation GI ad hoc committee (Hughes M, Cricchio AL, De Santis MC, et al.), Journal of Scleroderma and Related Disorders 11(1):e000024 (doi 10.1136/jsrd-2026-000024), 'Expert recommendations for the management of refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease in systemic sclerosis: A report from the World Scleroderma Foundation (WSF) Gastrointestinal 'Ad hoc committee'', published 1 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13271578/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Organise care (S2 Table 1):** severe or refractory SSc reflux belongs with a dedicated multidisciplinary team that includes gastroenterologists experienced in SSc gut disease and nutrition support (92.9% approval). Agree with gastroenterology when to repeat tests such as gastroscopy or pH monitoring. Symptoms alone cannot tell whether dysmotility or an incompetent lower oesophageal sphincter is driving refractory reflux (100%).
claims.locator: World Scleroderma Foundation GI ad hoc committee (Hughes M, Cricchio AL, De Santis MC, et al.), Journal of Scleroderma and Related Disorders 11(1):e000024 (doi 10.1136/jsrd-2026-000024), 'Expert recommendations for the management of refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease in systemic sclerosis: A report from the World Scleroderma Foundation (WSF) Gastrointestinal 'Ad hoc committee'', published 1 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13271578/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Review other drugs:** calcium channel blockers and other vasodilators for Raynaud's can worsen reflux by lowering lower oesophageal sphincter tone. Check that PPIs are taken about 30 minutes before meals.
claims.locator: World Scleroderma Foundation GI ad hoc committee (Hughes M, Cricchio AL, De Santis MC, et al.), Journal of Scleroderma and Related Disorders 11(1):e000024 (doi 10.1136/jsrd-2026-000024), 'Expert recommendations for the management of refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease in systemic sclerosis: A report from the World Scleroderma Foundation (WSF) Gastrointestinal 'Ad hoc committee'', published 1 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13271578/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Test objectively:** examine the mucosa in everyone with refractory symptoms, and strongly consider high-resolution manometry (particularly with dysphagia) and pH-impedance monitoring on a PPI to link symptoms to acid exposure. If manometry is not tolerated, scintigraphy or a timed barium swallow can screen for dysmotility.
claims.locator: World Scleroderma Foundation GI ad hoc committee (Hughes M, Cricchio AL, De Santis MC, et al.), Journal of Scleroderma and Related Disorders 11(1):e000024 (doi 10.1136/jsrd-2026-000024), 'Expert recommendations for the management of refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease in systemic sclerosis: A report from the World Scleroderma Foundation (WSF) Gastrointestinal 'Ad hoc committee'', published 1 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13271578/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Test for Helicobacter pylori and eradicate it if present.** It does not cause reflux, but long-term acid suppression in people carrying it raises the risk of gastric atrophy.
claims.locator: World Scleroderma Foundation GI ad hoc committee (Hughes M, Cricchio AL, De Santis MC, et al.), Journal of Scleroderma and Related Disorders 11(1):e000024 (doi 10.1136/jsrd-2026-000024), 'Expert recommendations for the management of refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease in systemic sclerosis: A report from the World Scleroderma Foundation (WSF) Gastrointestinal 'Ad hoc committee'', published 1 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13271578/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Night-time reflux:** raise the head of the bed, leave a longer gap between dinner and bed, and lie on the left side. Keep up weight control, stopping smoking and avoiding large, fatty or spicy meals throughout the disease.
claims.locator: World Scleroderma Foundation GI ad hoc committee (Hughes M, Cricchio AL, De Santis MC, et al.), Journal of Scleroderma and Related Disorders 11(1):e000024 (doi 10.1136/jsrd-2026-000024), 'Expert recommendations for the management of refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease in systemic sclerosis: A report from the World Scleroderma Foundation (WSF) Gastrointestinal 'Ad hoc committee'', published 1 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13271578/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **High-dose PPI is the first-line drug strategy for refractory SSc reflux,** a move away from H2 blockers, which often failed. Weigh the risks when osteoporosis, electrolyte disturbance, bacterial overgrowth or infection risk is high; heavy PPI exposure is linked with more severe calcinosis, and potassium-competitive acid blockers have similar side effects.
claims.locator: World Scleroderma Foundation GI ad hoc committee (Hughes M, Cricchio AL, De Santis MC, et al.), Journal of Scleroderma and Related Disorders 11(1):e000024 (doi 10.1136/jsrd-2026-000024), 'Expert recommendations for the management of refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease in systemic sclerosis: A report from the World Scleroderma Foundation (WSF) Gastrointestinal 'Ad hoc committee'', published 1 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13271578/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Add-ons when a PPI alone is not enough or cannot be increased:** an H2 blocker, a promotility drug or an alginate. With refractory reflux and dysphagia, strongly consider a trial of a promotility drug (prucalopride, pyridostigmine, domperidone or metoclopramide); vomiting, early satiety, post-meal pain or bloating also favour one.
claims.locator: World Scleroderma Foundation GI ad hoc committee (Hughes M, Cricchio AL, De Santis MC, et al.), Journal of Scleroderma and Related Disorders 11(1):e000024 (doi 10.1136/jsrd-2026-000024), 'Expert recommendations for the management of refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease in systemic sclerosis: A report from the World Scleroderma Foundation (WSF) Gastrointestinal 'Ad hoc committee'', published 1 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13271578/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Further options:** buspirone for a hypotensive lower oesophageal sphincter (stop it if a 2–4 week trial does not help); baclofen when pH-impedance shows mostly weakly acidic or non-acid reflux with a positive symptom link; an anti-emetic (ondansetron, promethazine, mirtazapine) for nausea that promotility drugs do not settle. Immunosuppression has no firm evidence for SSc gut disease.
claims.locator: World Scleroderma Foundation GI ad hoc committee (Hughes M, Cricchio AL, De Santis MC, et al.), Journal of Scleroderma and Related Disorders 11(1):e000024 (doi 10.1136/jsrd-2026-000024), 'Expert recommendations for the management of refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease in systemic sclerosis: A report from the World Scleroderma Foundation (WSF) Gastrointestinal 'Ad hoc committee'', published 1 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13271578/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Endoscopic anti-reflux procedures have little evidence** and are unsuitable with a large (over 3 cm) hiatal hernia. Surgery such as Nissen fundoplication is a last resort for highly selected patients, but may matter when upper-GI disease threatens eligibility for a life-saving lung transplant.
claims.locator: World Scleroderma Foundation GI ad hoc committee (Hughes M, Cricchio AL, De Santis MC, et al.), Journal of Scleroderma and Related Disorders 11(1):e000024 (doi 10.1136/jsrd-2026-000024), 'Expert recommendations for the management of refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease in systemic sclerosis: A report from the World Scleroderma Foundation (WSF) Gastrointestinal 'Ad hoc committee'', published 1 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13271578/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **With lung disease (SSc-ILD),** screen for aspiration (a modified barium swallow if there is proximal dysphagia, or coughing with meals or on lying flat), optimise reflux treatment, and test high-risk patients for silent reflux. **With overlapping myositis,** screen for pharyngeal involvement; IV immunoglobulin 2 g/kg a month, split over several days, may greatly help pharyngeal myositis.
claims.locator: World Scleroderma Foundation GI ad hoc committee (Hughes M, Cricchio AL, De Santis MC, et al.), Journal of Scleroderma and Related Disorders 11(1):e000024 (doi 10.1136/jsrd-2026-000024), 'Expert recommendations for the management of refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease in systemic sclerosis: A report from the World Scleroderma Foundation (WSF) Gastrointestinal 'Ad hoc committee'', published 1 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13271578/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **For symptomatic small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, give intermittent broad-spectrum oral antibiotics** (for example ciprofloxacin), possibly rotating agents; rifaximin is an option when refractory. (2B, 95%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Stop a fluoroquinolone at the first sign of a serious adverse reaction**, such as tendon pain or inflammation.
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diarrhoea and constipation often alternate**: treat symptomatically with antidiarrhoeals (for example loperamide) or laxatives, after excluding non-SSc causes. (1C, 96%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pelvic floor physiotherapy with anorectal biofeedback** may help selected patients with incontinence. (2C, 91%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider parenteral nutrition for severe weight loss or malnutrition (including high risk) that does not respond to enteral supplements.** (1B, 97%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Children with juvenile SSc:** actively assess and monitor nutrition, growth and puberty, and manage faltering growth with tertiary paediatric gastroenterology and dietetic input. (1C, 99%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Operate on GI complications only when essential and there is no alternative.** (1C, 97%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23
